predicted_responses.block_width_um: d(area)/d(w) = 2 x block_length_um = 1.775796 um2/um (two blocks, full length)
predicted_responses.arm_gap_um: d(delta_length)/d(gap) = tan(branch_angle/2) = 0.638 um/um (measured -0.032 for +0.05); area response is small because in the anisotropic gate frame the branch runs at 65 deg, so area is NOT width x length for a transverse knob
predicted_responses.loop_half_length_um: d(area)/d(half_len) = 4 x loop_wall_width_um (adding d to the half-length adds 2d of guide to EACH of the two loop halves) plus a saturating second term 2 x stem_width_um x min(d, stem_root_x - cavity_half_length) from the stem becoming exposed as the cavity tip slides out from under it. At the gate's default delta_um=5.0 the second term is saturated at 0.2345 um2, so measured 10.7185 vs predicted 10.4882 = 2.2% -> ok.

notes.why_spec_verify_fails: homi.spec_optimization.verify_knob_response demands d(delta_length_um)/d(knob) == 1 exactly - the MZI delta_length convention. This device is a loop-plus-bridge whose two vertices are pinned by the loop, so every INLINE change cancels and no knob moves a path length 1:1; arm_gap_um is the only path-length knob and it moves delta_length by tan(theta/2) = 0.638 per um. The area half of that check is also frame-limited (see above). The conductor's own area-only check (homi.conductor.gate.knob_response, entries A-C) passes with the geometrically predicted coefficients.

recommended_gate_knob.why: homi.conductor.gate.verify_cell perturbs by delta_um=5.0 by default. On a 3.0 x 5.5 um device only a loop-length knob stays in its linear geometric regime at that size; block/slot/arm knobs are exact at delta_um<=0.05 (entries A-C) but at +5 um the blocks would be 6 um tall and self-intersect.
